text: With the newest update (The Unseen) this finally feels like a true successor to Hades 1. It is substantially meatier, carries over what worked while putting in a new spin on just about every concept that needed it.  Things addressed included (in order of importance): 1: visual clutter and visibility: Definitely my biggest issue with H2 and so many small changes have made it so much easier to see when to dodge and where to stand! Only outstanding problem area is currently the boss of surface 1 with his sputtering dark red fast moving hitboxes, which is unfortunately even worse with the new affix (this isn't a huge issue since he's pretty easy, but kind of an annoying fight). 2: weapon/boon balance: the skull and macarenas finally feel as powerful and intuitive to use as the others. Hestia was brought up to speed with the rest and Ares was toned down(probably a bit too much for my liking, loved new release Ares but I get it). There's many other such changes but those were the stand out ones for me. 3: Gathering system/grind: It was heavily simplified and that's definitely for the best, makes even failed runs rewarding. 4: Not really an issue worked on but they added more and more content and finished what  was unfinished, to the point where the game feels quite rich and full.   Be advised there is still not a full story ending though, so you'll have blue balls on that till 1.0, especially if you play through at a fast clip.  Things that bug me that probably aren't addressable. 1. I don't think Mel and her relationship with the world is quite as interesting as Zagreus', which unfortunately really drags the story down as it's harder to get invested. She just kind of feels like a soldier doing her job. 2. Aesthetically I think I much preferred the look of H1, although I certainly appreciate them trying something a bit more witchy and different and it is basically objectively quite good art. 4. The boss of the surface doesn't quite measure up to the boss of the underworld as a fight, although it certainly is epic. 5. The path of stars alternates between being extremely powerful or so weak you have a hard time remembering it's there. Seems tough to balance.  Other: While there's alot to the decorating system it's just not that exciting, seems like there was an effort to make it all lore friendly which feels like a mistake. Having really goofy special ways to dress up the coven would be an excellent reward for challenging runs that would do nothing to disrupt game balance.

text: After spending a lot of time with both Hades and Hades II, I can confidently say that Hades II feels like a natural evolution of the first game. While Hades I still has the stronger emotional story and a more challenging experience, Hades II improves a lot of things in terms of gameplay, variety, and overall content.  One of the first things I noticed was the art direction, The designs of several gods and goddesses that already appeared in the first game like Aphrodite, Poseidon, and Athena feel more polished and refreshed in Hades II. The new characters also have a very unique visual identity that fits perfectly with the darker and more mystical atmosphere of the game.   The addition of the Arcana system makes a  huge difference build possibilities, and more strategic combat options make every run feel more interesting. The inclusion of pets and the ability to grow resources through planting and gathering also adds a new layer of progression that was not present in the first game.  Another huge improvement is the variety of encounters, Hades II gives you the opportunity to travel through both the Underworld and the Surface. Because of that, the enemies, environments, and challenges feel much more diverse. Every area feels like it has its own identity, and the new enemies and bosses keep the experience fresh.   From my personal experience, I also feel that Hades II is more approachable compared to the first game. Hades I felt more punishing and hardcore, especially when you were still learning enemy patterns and builds. Hades II feels more balanced and gives players more tools to survive. Of course, it can still be challenging, but the overall progression feels smoother.  The music is another area where Hades II improves. Hades I already had an amazing soundtrack with a stronger rock and intense atmosphere, but Hades II offers a wider variety of music styles. The soundtrack feels more mysterious, magical, and fitting with Melinoë's journey. It gives the game a completely different identity while still feeling like a Hades game.  However, when it comes to story and character development, I still think Hades I has the advantage. Zagreus' journey, his relationship with Hades, Nyx, Achilles, Thanatos, and other characters felt more personal and emotionally impactful. Hades II has many interesting characters and a bigger story, but for me, the first game had a stronger emotional connection.  Overall, I think Hades II is a better game mechanically. It improves the combat, adds more variety, and gives players more things to do. But Hades I still wins in terms of difficulty and storytelling. If you loved the first game, Hades II is definitely a must-play.

text: Within 24 hours this weekend, I played this game for 14 hours.  This game is different, but as good as the original, even now. I love how access to the game's mechanics is earlier in the game, and how this game emphasizes more balanced builds over overly synergistic builds.  The game has DPS checks, movement checks, but also the new charge attack system and mana system adds a layer of depth. Unlike Hades 1, charge attacks aren't something you specialize in, they're a resource fueled damage boost, and normal attack bonuses apply to them.  Using mana as a resource is KEY to cutting down enemies in reasonable times, as enemies are indeed spongier. However, using mana, your damage potential absolutely compensates for higher enemy health. Because of these changes, overall DPS and varied boons are a much higher priority than abusing synergies and using attacks as status sticks and damage sticks.  Positioning is key, and working around Mel's differing movement mechanics actually makes certain bosses like the Region 3 boss incredibly hectic. Being limited to one dash really makes you appreciate the sprint mechanics and makes you use dashes not for movement, but solely for dodging. At first a lack of dodge chains felt like a downgrade, but as I got more used to it, it made me feel much more in control of my exact position, and bosses have much larger AoEs to necessitate good positioning skills. Charge attacks can and should be used as extra movement/ranged options when necessary.  The new weapons feel great, I don't like the twin torches much, however I don't think they've properly clicked with me, but the staff, sister blades, and the axe are amazing, and I love how the Argent Skull provides a fully fledged weapon variant of the old cast system from the first game, alongside the grenades from the Adamant Rail.  Also, I've heard this game has great potential for modding, and judging by the first game's modability, I forsee a modding community for the games sprouting up sometime soon. I look forward to seeing what the community does to the games.

text: [b] TL;DR: [/b] Combat and build variety are solid and runs are still addictive. But the story’s second half feels kinda rushed and never reaches the emotional payoff of Hades. Still a very fun roguelite and definitely worth a run.  [b] Let me give a quick heads up first: This review contains partial spoilers. [/b]  I’ll be honest, I still can’t quite decide whether this game is an upgrade or a downgrade compared to the first one. There are moments where it feels genuinely brilliant, and others where certain choices really make you miss the original. Maybe my memory is playing tricks on me and I’m overhyping the first game. Either way, one thing is certain: I can never say no to a Supergiant Games title. Even with the criticisms I’m about to mention, Hades II is a game I genuinely enjoyed and poured hours into. Don’t hesitate to give it a chance, whether you take my review into account or someone else’s.  I’m no art expert, but the game’s art direction and environments looked fantastic to me. When I launched it for the first time, I literally thought, “Wow, I really missed the atmosphere of Hades 1.” As much as I enjoyed the soundtrack, it felt a bit less impactful than the first game overall. That said, it still had its moments. Like when I ended up fighting Zagreus in Elysium and The Unseen Ones (from the first game) kicked in. I practically ascended. You can still hear echoes of the first game’s songs in some tracks, and honestly, I still think Darren Korb did a solid job with what they had to work with this time around.  One of the biggest issues, and something many people have already pointed out, is the second half of the story. It starts off feeling like a serious oath of vengeance, but the further you go the more it unravels and turns into something almost comical. It genuinely feels like the writers just went, “Well, here’s the ending, I guess.” The dialogue in that section feels oddly unserious too, and it doesn’t come anywhere near the emotional punch of Hades 1’s Epilogue. I didn’t personally notice any major plot holes, but it did feel rushed, like it was written with a “good enough, ship it” mindset. And no, I don’t think it felt bland only because of this era of rapid content consumption. A mid story on its own wouldn’t bother me, but this one had so much potential that it ended up feeling disappointing.  That said, I actually really liked Melinoe as a character. She carries the seriousness of her role well, she’s likable, and she’s easily one of the better-written characters in the cast. Without going too deep into spoilers, the character development we see throughout the first half of the game basically gets slam-dunked into a trash can in an instant. A character written this well deserved a much better ending. So while I enjoyed parts of the story, overall it fell short of my expectations.  The spirits whose fates we can influence also left me a bit disappointed. None of them felt as well-written or emotionally impactful as Eurydice and Orpheus, and the fact that we now have characters who clearly resemble that duo just makes the comparison unavoidable. That said, the dialogue and character interactions didn’t bother me too much. Some exchanges even managed to get a laugh out of me.  One thing that genuinely upset me is that once you reach a certain point in the story, you can never return to Olympus or the House of Hades. Even something as simple as listening to Apollo’s music after a run would have been enough to motivate players to keep coming back. If we could return to the House of Hades, spend time with family members, hear Orpheus perform songs from the first game, or just chat with Underworld characters, maybe the second half wouldn’t have felt so empty. And seriously, where did Hypnos go? After working so hard to wake that poor guy up, not seeing him at all was honestly kind of sad.  Gameplay-wise and content-wise, I can confidently say the game builds on the original. There are small additions everywhere, and overall it feels rich in content. I liked Melinoe’s abilities and some of the new weapon aspects. The only downside is that some of those aspects unlock very late, so a lot of players might shelve the game before even getting to try them. Still, I think there’s enough weapon variety, and I don’t really see this as a game meant to be played endlessly like some other rogue-lites.  I didn’t experiment much with different builds during my playtime, but I will say this: many of the new god boons felt unnecessary, and I ignored them pretty often. Once I grabbed the few boons I personally liked and considered strong, nothing else really mattered. And unlike the first game, I didn’t find a build that let me wipe everything just by dashing. Could be a skill issue, who knows xD  All in all, despite its flaws, it’s a game I can comfortably recommend. I just wish they had spent more time polishing the story instead of rushing toward a full release. With a bit more time, I genuinely believe they could have delivered something truly great. And honestly, many players, myself included, wouldn’t have minded waiting longer.  If you actually read all this yapping, thank you so much. Take care, fren.

Still a very fun roguelite and definitely worth a run.  [b] Let me give a quick heads up first: This review contains partial spoilers. [/b]  I’ll be honest, I still can’t quite decide whether this game is an upgrade or a downgrade compared to the first one. There are moments where it feels genuinely brilliant, and others where certain choices really make you miss the original. Maybe my memory is playing tricks on me and I’m overhyping the first game. Either way, one thing is certain: I can never say no to a Supergiant Games title. Even with the criticisms I’m about to mention, Hades II is a game I genuinely enjoyed and poured hours into. Don’t hesitate to give it a chance, whether you take my review into account or someone else’s.  I’m no art expert, but the game’s art direction and environments looked fantastic to me. When I launched it for the first time, I literally thought, “Wow, I really missed the atmosphere of Hades 1.” As much as I enjoyed the soundtrack, it felt a bit less impactful than the first game overall. That said, it still had its moments. Like when I ended up fighting Zagreus in Elysium and The Unseen Ones (from the first game) kicked in. I practically ascended. You can still hear echoes of the first game’s songs in some tracks, and honestly, I still think Darren Korb did a solid job with what they had to work with this time around.  One of the biggest issues, and something many people have already pointed out, is the second half of the story. It starts off feeling like a serious oath of vengeance, but the further you go the more it unravels and turns into something almost comical. It genuinely feels like the writers just went, “Well, here’s the ending, I guess.” The dialogue in that section feels oddly unserious too, and it doesn’t come anywhere near the emotional punch of Hades 1’s Epilogue. I didn’t personally notice any major plot holes, but it did feel rushed, like it was written with a “good enough, ship it” mindset. And no, I don’t think it felt bland only because of this era of rapid content consumption. A mid story on its own wouldn’t bother me, but this one had so much potential that it ended up feeling disappointing.  That said, I actually really liked Melinoe as a character. She carries the seriousness of her role well, she’s likable, and she’s easily one of the better-written characters in the cast. Without going too deep into spoilers, the character development we see throughout the first half of the game basically gets slam-dunked into a trash can in an instant. A character written this well deserved a much better ending. So while I enjoyed parts of the story, overall it fell short of my expectations.  The spirits whose fates we can influence also left me a bit disappointed. None of them felt as well-written or emotionally impactful as Eurydice and Orpheus, and the fact that we now have characters who clearly resemble that duo just makes the comparison unavoidable. That said, the dialogue and character interactions didn’t bother me too much. Some exchanges even managed to get a laugh out of me.  One thing that genuinely upset me is that once you reach a certain point in the story, you can never return to Olympus or the House of Hades. Even something as simple as listening to Apollo’s music after a run would have been enough to motivate players to keep coming back. If we could return to the House of Hades, spend time with family members, hear Orpheus perform songs from the first game, or just chat with Underworld characters, maybe the second half wouldn’t have felt so empty. And seriously, where did Hypnos go? After working so hard to wake that poor guy up, not seeing him at all was honestly kind of sad.  Gameplay-wise and content-wise, I can confidently say the game builds on the original. There are small additions everywhere, and overall it feels rich in content. I liked Melinoe’s abilities and some of the new weapon aspects. The only downside is that some of those aspects unlock very late, so a lot of players might shelve the game before even getting to try them. Still, I think there’s enough weapon variety, and I don’t really see this as a game meant to be played endlessly like some other rogue-lites.  I didn’t experiment much with different builds during my playtime, but I will say this: many of the new god boons felt unnecessary, and I ignored them pretty often. Once I grabbed the few boons I personally liked and considered strong, nothing else really mattered. And unlike the first game, I didn’t find a build that let me wipe everything just by dashing. Could be a skill issue, who knows xD  All in all, despite its flaws, it’s a game I can comfortably recommend. I just wish they had spent more time polishing the story instead of rushing toward a full release. With a bit more time, I genuinely believe they could have delivered something truly great. And honestly, many players, myself included, wouldn’t have minded waiting longer.  If you actually read all this yapping, thank you so much. Take care, fren.
